To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the Markov property is a useful concept for the analysis of the topological characteristics in correlated random networks; (2) Markovian networks are fully characterized solely through the two-point degree correlations among nodes and (3) real Internet topologies are not necessarily Markovian.

(1) we introduce a new class of random networks called the Markovian random networks, (2) we derive the analytical formulas of graph theoretical metrics for Markovian random network, (3) we show that the Internet topologies are not in the class of Markovian random graphs, and (4) we show that it is rather impossible to characterize the Internet topologies solely by two-point correlation.
(1) the Internet topologies are non-Markovian, and (2) the Markov property is not suitable for modeling Internet topologies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the introduction of the concept of the Markov network, and its application to modeling and analysis of the Internet topologies.

the development of a framework for the analysis of the topological characteristics in terms of the two-point and higher-order degree correlation, and the investigation of the Markov properties of the Internet topologies.
the introduction of the concept of the Markov chain to the study of complex networks, with the aim of finding a maximally unbiased network under the constraint of prescribed correlation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Markovian property can serve as a good indicator of the degree of the correlation among the nodes in a network.
the Internet is not Markovian, which implies that the Markovian assumption is not appropriate to describe the topological characteristics at AS- and router level.
the Markov property is a necessary, but not sufficient condition for the Internet topologies to be unbiased.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Markov property is a necessary condition for the existence of the maximally unbiased networks, and that the Markovian property can be a powerful tool for the characterization of the network topologies.
the Markovian framework can be a useful tool for modeling the Internet topologies.
the Markov property is not satisfied for the Internet topologies, and that it would be necessary to introduce higher-order correlations in order to fully characterize them.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Markov property of a random network is an indispensable property to model the network topologies in a way to be unbiased with respect to higher-order degree correlation.
the Markovian framework is useful for the analysis of the topological characteristics and the evolution of real-world networks.
the Markov property can be used as a criterion to assess the degree of correlation in the Internet topologies.
